title: Tyco MINERVA MX / MX2
scope: Manufacturer 17A-05-O Issue 5 (11/04), Firmware Version 5.0. Documented shared MX/MX2 paths only; later firmware and undocumented service menus are not claimed.

event-print.summary: This option requires a configured printer. Choose destination, range and lowest priority, then F5 Print. FINDR records a simulated print only.

event-filter.summary: Toggle any of categories 1–9; + marks a selection. F4 View shows matching entries; F5 Print uses the configured printer.

point-values.summary: Choose panel where networked, loop and address, then F5 Enter. View the programmed type, detected type/mode and reported sensor value. F5 Print prints the selected loop, not just this point.

faults.title: View Faults
faults.label: View Faults

faults.summary: This option is view only. Read fault point references and use View Status to inspect a specific programmed device; a displayed fault is not a cable-location proof.

loop-counters.title: Loop Point Counters
loop-counters.label: Loop Point Counters
loop-counters.hint: Select panel where networked and loop, then F5 Enter. The source describes an approximately two-minute real scan. PASSED requires matching configured/detected counts, no unconfigured points and equal left/right/both counts. FINDR uses an explicitly synthetic immediate result.
loop-counters.summary: Select panel where networked and loop, then F5 Enter. The source describes an approximately two-minute real scan. PASSED requires matching configured/detected counts, no unconfigured points and equal left/right/both counts. FINDR uses an explicitly synthetic immediate result.

loop-details.title: Details
loop-details.label: Details
loop-details.hint: From Loop Point Counters press F2 Details. F2 >> pages all 250 addresses: o connected/configured/identified, c configured but not connected/identified, u connected but not configured. These are addresses, never physical cable sequence.
loop-details.summary: From Loop Point Counters press F2 Details. F2 >> pages all 250 addresses: o connected/configured/identified, c configured but not connected/identified, u connected but not configured. These are addresses, never physical cable sequence.

loop-scan.title: Scan
loop-scan.label: Scan
loop-scan.hint: From Loop Point Counters press F3 Scan. F2 >> pages addresses: . empty, * seen from both sides, l left only, r right only. This is an investigation aid and cannot establish physical cable order or a break location.
loop-scan.summary: From Loop Point Counters press F3 Scan. F2 >> pages addresses: . empty, * seen from both sides, l left only, r right only. This is an investigation aid and cannot establish physical cable order or a break location.

walk-test.title: Walk Test
walk-test.label: Walk Test
walk-test.hint: Select the exact scope before F5 Start; only one session may run. F3 Settings reviews the chosen scope. F5 End is allowed only once all selected points are inactive. Keep alarm/monitoring arrangements and restoration explicit.
walk-test.summary: Select the exact scope before F5 Start; only one session may run. F3 Settings reviews the chosen scope. F5 End is allowed only once all selected points are inactive. Keep alarm/monitoring arrangements and restoration explicit.
notes: Panel field only on a network. Point scope uses Location Loop, Zone and Point.
Automatic self-test applies only to detector type; the manual lists 801PH, 801CH and 801I. Lasertest is not used.
Sounder test pulses selected sounders and displays no results. Full multisensor test requires both sensing modes; Part depends on configured active modes.
Isolated points are excluded. Ending the session is blocked while any selected input remains active.

alarm-count.title: Fire Alarm Cycle Count
alarm-count.label: Fire Alarm Cycle Count

alarm-count.summary: View the number of fire-alarm sequences. This number is a historic counter, not evidence that a current fault is repaired.

text-point.title: Point Text
text-point.label: Point Text
text-point.hint: Select the target. F2 >> copies old text; F3 − / F4 + moves the cursor. Use the alphanumeric keypad; Up selects capitals, Down lower case. F5 Enter asks Save Data? F4 Yes stages the change; F5 No returns to editing. Commit through Configuration → 9 Restart before leaving.

notes: The source contains occasional wording errors calling Change Text’s submenu “Configuration”; the illustrated menu hierarchy establishes the parent path.

nodes.hint: Select the target. F2 >> copies old text; F3 − / F4 + moves the cursor. Use the alphanumeric keypad; Up selects capitals, Down lower case. F5 Enter asks Save Data? F4 Yes stages the change; F5 No returns to editing. Commit through Configuration → 9 Restart before leaving.

nodes.title: Restart
nodes.label: Restart
nodes.hint: Shown only after saved text changes. Commit with Configuration → 9 Restart. Do not use Back while Restart is showing and do not edit multiple network panels in one session. The manual directs ENABLE off to abandon changes instead of Back.

nodes.title: Test Buzzer, LEDs & Display
nodes.label: Test Buzzer, LEDs & Display
nodes.hint: Tests the buzzer, indicator LEDs and LCD. The source also allows this test without ENABLE through the home LED Tst softkey; do not confuse it with a device walk test.

physicalKeys.label: ENABLE 0 / I
physicalKeys.hint: 0 normal; I enable. Operator 1 needs no passcode. Higher profiles are site-configured.

physicalKeys.label: F1–F5 softkeys
physicalKeys.hint: Each key performs the action printed immediately above it; labels change with the current screen.

physicalKeys.label: 0–9 alphanumeric keypad
physicalKeys.hint: Numbers select numbered menu options; repeated digits enter letters during text editing.

physicalKeys.label: Scroll up / down
physicalKeys.hint: Scroll entries/logs; upper/lower case during configuration text editing.

physicalKeys.label: SILENCE BUZZER
physicalKeys.hint: Silences the local buzzer; it does not clear the alarm/fault cause.

physicalKeys.label: SILENCE / RESOUND
physicalKeys.hint: Toggles the external sounder state under the permitted access profile.

physicalKeys.label: RESET
physicalKeys.hint: Reset only after the event has been investigated; an active cause may recur.

physicalKeys.label: DAY / NIGHT
physicalKeys.hint: Changes the configured day/night mode; effects depend on the site configuration.

physicalKeys.label: INVESTIGATE DELAY
physicalKeys.hint: Ends the signalling delay and starts the configured investigation time; it is not an unrestricted silence control.

physicalKeys.label: EVACUATE
physicalKeys.hint: Activates configured external sounders in the training simulation only.

physicalKeys.label: FUNCTION / SPARE
physicalKeys.hint: Site-defined. The MX2 figure shows FUNCTION, but the prose says it excludes SPARE; this source discrepancy is shown as reference-only rather than assigning an invented action.

lessons.title: Find the event history
lessons.summary: Locate recent events and filter faults without clearing their cause.
prerequisites: Training simulation only; verify the actual panel firmware and site access profile.

steps.title: Enable and sign in
steps.instruction: Turn ENABLE on; use the explicitly labelled practice profile for Customer Operator 3 or above.

steps.title: Open the log
steps.instruction: Main menu 5 Event Log → 1 View Event Log.

steps.title: Browse or filter
steps.instruction: Use the log softkeys. Back to 3 Filter; select 5 Fault, then F4 View.

lessons.title: Find a programmed device
lessons.summary: Read the panel’s programmed location for an exact loop/address.
prerequisites: Training simulation only; verify the actual panel firmware and site access profile.

steps.title: Open View Status
steps.instruction: Main menu 2 View Status → 1 Point → 1 Loop Point.

steps.title: Select exact fields
steps.instruction: Use >> / − / + and Enter; check panel number if networked, loop and point.

steps.title: Read scope correctly
steps.instruction: Read zone/location/type/status together. Configuration text is not proof of installed device or physical cable order.

lessons.title: Isolate and restore a loop point
lessons.summary: Practise a deliberate single-point isolation and its restoration.
prerequisites: Training simulation only; verify the actual panel firmware and site access profile.

steps.title: Establish scope
steps.instruction: Agree the real-site authorisation/monitoring arrangements before impairing protection. Use Operator 6 or higher in training.

steps.title: Choose a point
steps.instruction: Main menu 3 → 1 Point → 1 Loop Point, then select its address.

steps.title: Isolate and restore
steps.instruction: 1 Isolate changes the chosen simulated point; 2 De-Isolate restores it. Check the isolation count.

lessons.title: Start and finish a walk test
lessons.summary: Practise the test scope and the active-point end guard.
prerequisites: Training simulation only; verify the actual panel firmware and site access profile.

steps.title: Select a session
steps.instruction: Main menu 7 Service → 1 Walk Test. Only one session can run.

steps.title: Set scope and start
steps.instruction: Choose panel/area/type/loop as applicable, then F5 Start.

steps.title: Finish and restore
steps.instruction: F3 Settings reviews scope. Make selected points inactive, then F5 End. Record restoration on the real job.

lessons.title: Find battery and charger readings
lessons.summary: Find the panel-reported battery state without inventing a pass/fail limit.
prerequisites: Training simulation only; verify the actual panel firmware and site access profile.

steps.title: Open maintenance
steps.instruction: Use a Customer Manager profile. Main menu 7 → 2 Maintenance → 4 Battery Test.

steps.title: Read the three values
steps.instruction: Read battery state, battery voltage and charger current. Manual example values are not acceptance thresholds.

lessons.title: Find loop counter and side-scan diagnostics
lessons.summary: Use configured/detected counts and left/right scans as an investigation aid.
prerequisites: Training simulation only; verify the actual panel firmware and site access profile.

steps.title: Open counters
steps.instruction: Customer Manager 2: Main menu 6 View/Print Data → 5 Loop Point Counters.

steps.title: Select panel and loop
steps.instruction: Choose the correct network panel and loop, then Enter. The real panel scan takes approximately two minutes.

steps.title: Inspect Details and Scan
steps.instruction: F2 Details shows o/c/u configuration states; F3 Scan shows */l/r detection. Never infer cable sequence from addresses.

lessons.title: Change and commit a location label
lessons.summary: Practise the documented staged text-save/restart sequence.
prerequisites: Training simulation only; verify the actual panel firmware and site access profile.

steps.title: Open point text
steps.instruction: Customer Manager: 8 Configuration → 1 Change Text → 1 Point Text.

steps.title: Edit and stage
steps.instruction: Select the loop/point, edit the text, Enter, then F4 Yes at Save Data?.

steps.title: Commit correctly
steps.instruction: Back to Configuration, use 9 Restart. Do not Back out of Configuration with pending changes or change multiple panels in one session.

boundaries.reason: Diagnostics entry is drawn, but no diagnostic submenu or procedure is supplied.
Software Initialisation Count readout/reset described, but its numbered menu selector is not stated.
This source explicitly states Firmware Version 5.0; newer versions must be checked against their own documents.
Only Change Text and its conditional Restart are documented. Adding/deleting devices and full project configuration are not in this manual.
MX2 diagram shows FUNCTION while prose excludes SPARE. No unsupported action is assigned.
The Maintenance illustration shows a Total/Print readout instead of numbered menu labels. Only explicitly stated numbers are used.
The p23 menu illustration omits option5; p24 explicitly says select5 and p17 restricts it to CustomerManager2.
Table 1 marks View/print status from Operator4 but its ViewFaults row from Operator3. The parent retains the stricter documented Operator4 entry; no lower-level shortcut is invented.
Counter and scan tables are indexed by address. The source does not establish physical cable order.
